sentences.text: ... RESPONDENTS Mr. K. S. Narwade, Advocate a/w Mr. Vishwa Gadbaile, Advocate for Appellant.
Mr. A. B. Patil, Advocate for Respondent No.3.

Mr. M. A. Kadu, AGP for Respondent Nos.1 and 2.
 CORAM :

PRAVIN S. PATIL, J.
 DATE : NOVEMBER 06, 2025.
JUDGMENT .

Heard Mr. K. S. Narwade, learned Counsel for the Appellant, Mr. A. B. Patil, learned Counsel for the Respondent No.3 and Mr. M. A. Kadu, learned AGP for the Respondent Nos.1 and 2.
2.
The challenge in the present Appeal is to the Judgment and Award dated 27/7/2009 passed in Land Acquisition Case No. 57/2005.
The Appellant herein is the original Claimant.
By way of this Appeal, he is seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the learned Reference Court.

According to him, though he has established before the Reference Court that 3/7 34.Judg.fa.356.2010.odt his land is an irrigated land, the learned Reference Court, without dealing with the matter properly and also by not appreciating the evidence available on record, has awarded less amount, and therefore, he filed the present Appeal before this Court.

3. The undisputed facts in the present matter is that, Respondent No.2, on 1/5/1997 issued Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act for acquisition of land for the purpose of submergence of Varadh Minor Irrigation Project.

Under the said acquisition proceeding, land owned by the Appellant bearing Gat No. 192, area admeasuring 1.37 HR situated at village Loni Bandar,
Tahsil Ralegaon, District Yavatmal has been acquired by the Respondents.
4. The Land Acquisition Officer has awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.12,000/- per hectare vide Award dated 22/8/2000.
As such, the Appellant has received compensation amount for the acquired land Rs.16,440/- and towards well Rs.1,03,570/-.

As such, total amount of compensation was awarded at Rs.1,30,532/-.
5.
It is the case of the Appellant before the Reference Court that his land being an irrigated land, he should have been awarded compensation at 4/7 34.Judg.fa.356.2010.odt the rate of Rs.2,00,000/-

2 per hectare.
To substantiate this fact, the Appellant has specifically pointed out that village Loni Bandar is adjacent to the village Varadh.
He has also pointed out that the land from village Varadh bearing Gat No. 31/4-A admeasuring 2.84 HR was acquired for the same project.
In the said matter this Court in First Appeal No. 1273/2019 decided on 11/9/2019 enhanced the compensation from Rs.1,00,000/- to Rs.2,00,000/- by considering the same as an irrigated land.
Hence, the Appellant claimed enhancement in the present Appeal on the ground of parity.
6. The learned Counsel for Respondent No.3 has strongly opposed the enhancement of compensation.

According to him, it was for the Appellant to demonstrate before the Reference Court that the adjoining land is having same potentiality and certain pains were required to be taken by the Appellant to establish the facts before the Reference Court, however, the Appellant failed to establish his case, and therefore, he is not entitled for any enhancement of compensation in the matter.

7. I have heard learned Counsel for both sides and gone through the record and case laws relied upon by them.
8.
From the record it is established that Appellant has led oral as 5/7 34.Judg.fa.356.2010.odt well as documentary evidence.
No evidence is adduced by the Respondent in the matter.
Village Loni Bandar and Varadh are adjacent to each other.

7/12 extract of the acquired land (Exhibit-42 to 44)
shows that Appellant used to take crops of cotton, tur, soyabean etc.
There was one well and entry of one oil engine on the said well.
Hence, acquired land was having irrigation facility.
So also from oral evidence it is clear that land was having road facility.
9. The Appellant has relied upon the Judgments in Land Acquisition Case Nos. 732/2002 and 740/2002, wherein compensation was granted Rs.1,00,000/- per hectare.
The said land was dry crop land whereas acquired land having well ought to have been considered as an irrigated land.

According to the Appellant though Reference Court recorded the finding that in the acquired land facility of water was available and considering the location of field, Appellant could have fetch more value, but awarded only Rs.1,00,000/- without any discussion as to why the Appellant is not entitled for compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- per hectare by treating the same as an irrigated land.

10. The Appellant has relied upon the Judgment of this Court in the case of State of Maharashtra V/s Baliram G. Patil, 2006(6) Mh.L.J. 72 and Chindha Fakira Patil V/s Special Land Acquisition Officer, 2012(2) Mh.L.J. 530 6/7 34.Judg.fa.356.2010.odt to state that irrigated land ought to be granted compensation at twice the rate of dry crop land.
11.

The Appellant has also relied upon the Judgment delivered by this Court in First Appeal No.
1273/2019 decided on 11/9/2019, wherein the land was located from village Varadh and acquired for same project and the Co- ordinate Bench of this Court has awarded compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- per hectare to the irrigated land.
12. The learned Counsel for both sides have admitted the fact that this Judgment dated 11/9/2019 passed in First Appeal No. 1273/2019 is till date holding the field.
This Judgment is not under Lalsing S/O Amaru Rathod (Dead) Thr. Lrs vs The State Of Maha.

3 challenge before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
As such, according to me, when this Court had taken a view and thereby decided the market value of the irrigated land, there is no reason for me to take another view in the matter.

13. As I have already held that the Appellant has established on record that the land acquired in question is an irrigated land and this fact is not disputed in the matter, I hold that Appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation at the rate of Rs.2,00,000/- per hectare.
In the circumstances, I proceed to pass following order.
7/7 34.Judg.f  ORDER  1.
First Appeal is allowed.
2. The impugned Judgment and order passed by the Reference Court is modified to the extent that Appellant is entitled for enhancement of Rs.2,00,000/- per hectare.
3. Rest of the Judgment and order passed by this Reference Court is confirmed.
4. The Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the enhanced amount of compensation with the Registry of this Court within a period of four months.

5. After deposit of the enhanced amount, the Appellant will be at liberty to withdraw the same,
subject to satisfaction of the Registrar (Judicial) of this Court.
6. No order as to costs.
